why: Diaphragm contraction and flattening increases thoracic volume, causing inspiration.

q: Most oxygen is transported in blood bound to:
why: The majority of O2 is carried bound to haemoglobin as oxyhaemoglobin.

q: About what percentage of CO2 produced by tissues is transported in blood as bicarbonate ions?
why: Roughly 70% of CO2 is carried as bicarbonate ions (HCO3-) in plasma.

q: The valve located between the right atrium and right ventricle of the human heart is the:
why: The tricuspid valve guards the opening between the right atrium and right ventricle.

q: Which heart chamber has the thickest muscular wall, since it pumps blood to the entire body?
why: The left ventricle has the thickest wall to generate high pressure for systemic circulation.

q: If stroke volume is 70 mL and heart rate is 72 beats/min, the cardiac output is approximately:
why: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate = 70 x 72 = 5040 mL/min ~= 5 L/min.

q: A person with blood group AB has no antibodies against A or B antigens, making this group the:
why: Group AB lacks anti-A and anti-B antibodies, so it can receive from any ABO group.

q: In an ECG, the QRS complex represents:
why: The sharp QRS complex corresponds to depolarization/contraction of the ventricles.

q: One complete cardiac cycle normally takes about:
why: A full cardiac cycle (atrial systole + ventricular systole + joint diastole) lasts about 0.8 s.

q: The heart sounds 'lub' and 'dup' are produced respectively by the closing of:
why: 'Lub' is from AV valve closure, 'dup' is from semilunar valve closure.
